what: Stryker makes medical equipment and implants: hip and knee replacements, spine products, surgical power tools, endoscopy systems, hospital beds and emergency equipment. Its Mako robot assists surgeons in joint replacement.
customers: Hospitals, surgical centres and emergency services in about 61 countries.
money: surgical instruments, endoscopy, hospital equipment and neurovascular devices
hip, knee and trauma implants, and the Mako surgical robot
moat: Surgeons trained on its instruments and robot, Mako systems installed in hospitals that then buy its implants, and a sales force that works inside operating theatres.
risks: Hospitals negotiate hard on implant prices
Return on invested capital is modest because of the price paid for acquisitions
Elective surgery volumes fall when hospitals are short of staff
Any recall in implants carries long-term liability
opportunities: An ageing population raises the number of joint replacements every year
Each Mako robot placed pulls years of implant sales behind it
Revenue has grown around 11% a year, faster than most large device makers
watch: Mako installations and organic growth in Orthopaedics, which shows whether the robot is winning implant share.
